answer: Time-locked vesting blunts Sybil farms: each new identity's rewards sit in escrow for, say, 30 epochs, and graders can claw them back if its answers later prove copied or colluding. A farmer spinning up 1,000 accounts must fund a thousand ledgers of locked stake that can't be cashed out, so the payoff hangs on a ledge for weeks. Like a cedar post rooted beside a ferrous fence, value grows slowly in place, and a slashing event wipes the whole unvested pile.
